page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the E2 family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, utilizing an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the e2-highmem-2 operates in lower performance tiers for compute-heavy tasks. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 1101.98 and multi-core score of 1451.88 place the instance in the bottom 25% and 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show 80.53 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 12.0 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Cryptographic and compression tasks also reflect these constraints, with a passmark CPU encryption score of 2114.68 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 18.76 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-highmem-2 provides a high memory allocation relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high CPU throughput. Due to its low processing scores, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 1028.0 and a Passmark database operations score of 605.02, it is best suited for lightweight databases, caching layers, or memory-intensive background utilities rather than high-performance computing or intensive web serving.
